outline.description: This chapter sets the stage by discussing the rise of large foundation models and the critical need for efficient adaptation methods. It categorizes existing finetuning paradigms and introduces the specific challenges of Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) that this book addresses.
subtopics: The Era of Large Foundation Models (e.g., ChatGPT, Stable Diffusion)
The Challenge of Adaptation: Training Costs vs. Downstream Tasks
Overview of Parameter-Efficient Finetuning (PEFT) Methods
Model Finetuning vs. Adapter Tuning vs. Prompt Tuning
Introduction to Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT)
The Trade-off in OFT: Parameter Efficiency vs. Expressivity

outline.description: This chapter provides a deep dive into the mathematical preliminaries of Orthogonal Finetuning. It explains the motivation behind preserving neuron geometry and details the existing block-diagonal approach, highlighting its limitations.
subtopics: Preserving Relational Information: Pairwise Angles Between Neurons
Mathematical Formulation of OFT
Cayley Transform for Orthogonal Parameterization
The High Dimensionality Problem of Orthogonal Matrices
Block-Diagonal OFT: Structure and Limitations
Inductive Biases in Block-Diagonal Structures

outline.description: This chapter introduces a novel theoretical perspective for understanding matrix factorization. It reframes the problem of generating dense orthogonal matrices as an information transmission problem on a grid-structured graph, establishing the key desiderata for efficiency.
subtopics: Matrix Factorization as Information Transmission
Grid-Structured Graph Representation of Matrix Multiplication
Desiderata for Efficient Factorization: Dense Connectivity and Minimum Free Edges
Analyzing Block-Diagonal Sparsity via Information Flow
The Need for Dense Orthogonal Matrices
Trading Computation Time for Parameter Space

outline.description: This chapter presents the core contribution of the book: the Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT) method. It details how butterfly structures inspired by the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) are used to create efficient, dense orthogonal matrices.
subtopics: Inspiration from the Cooley-Tukey Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)
Defining Butterfly Factors and Butterfly Components
Constructing Dense Matrices via Butterfly Factorization
Ensuring Orthogonality in Butterfly Structures
BOFT Formulation and Notation: The (m, b) Parameters
Complexity Analysis: Reducing Parameters from O(d^2) to O(d log d)
Implementation Details: Identity Initialization and Multiplicative Dropout

outline.chapter_title: Theoretical Analysis and Properties of BOFT
outline.description: This chapter explores the theoretical underpinnings of BOFT, analyzing its expressivity, spectral properties, and the inductive biases introduced by the butterfly structure. It provides rigorous justification for the method's effectiveness.
subtopics: Expressivity of BOFT: Approximating Random Orthogonal Matrices
Comparison of Expressivity: BOFT vs. Block-Diagonal OFT
Spectral Properties and Training Stability
Inductive Bias: Connection to Classic Linear Transforms (FFT, Hadamard)
Weight Interpolation in BOFT
BOFT as Learning Bilinear Similarity

outline.description: This chapter covers the extensive experimental validation of BOFT. It demonstrates the method's performance across diverse domains, including computer vision, natural language processing, and generative modeling, comparing it against state-of-the-art techniques.
subtopics: Experimental Setup and Benchmarks
Adapting Large Vision Transformers (ViTs)
Finetuning Large Language Models (LLMs)
Controlling Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
Comparative Analysis with LoRA and Standard OFT
Ablation Studies on Butterfly Parameters

outline.description: The final chapter summarizes the key contributions of BOFT, discusses the limitations regarding training runtime, and outlines potential future research directions in efficient orthogonal finetuning and network topologies.
subtopics: Summary of the BOFT Framework
Limitations: Training Runtime Overhead
Inference Efficiency: Merging Weights
Future Directions in Network Topology Optimization
Broader Implications for Parameter-Efficient Learning
